name: AUD is a Chronic Disease
content: Alcohol Use Disorder (AUD) is a chronic health condition that causes people to feel compelled to drink, to drink too much, and not be able to stop.

name: AUD is not a Choice
content: AUD is caused by a combination of biological, psychological, and environmental factors. Overcoming it is not just a matter of willpower or making better decisions.

name: AUD Doesn't Discriminate
content: AUD affects 18% of Canadians, age 15 and older, over their lifetime. It impacts people from all backgrounds, ages, and walks of life.

name: AUD Deserves Compassion
content: AUD is a medical condition. As such, it should be treated with compassion and without stigma.

items: Have there been periods when you ended up drinking more, or longer, than you intended?
Want to cut down or stop drinking, but couldn't?
Spend a lot of time drinking? Or being sick after drinking?
Want a drink so badly you couldn't think of anything else?
Find that drinking interfered with taking care of your home or family, or getting to work or school?
Continue to drink even though it was causing trouble with your family or friends?
Not go to activities that were important or interesting to you, in order to drink?
Get into hazardous situations during or after drinking that increased your chances of getting hurt?
Continue to drink even though it was affecting your health?
Find that your usual number of drinks had much less effect than before?
Find that you experienced withdrawal symptoms, such as trouble sleeping, shakiness, restlessness, or a racing heart?

content: In general, responding YES to 2-3 questions may indicate mild AUD; 4-5 may indicate moderate AUD; and 6+ may indicate severe AUD
